summary: AstroVita is an offline-first health companion for astronauts on deep-space missions. On a trip to Mars, radio messages take up to about 22 minutes one way, so crews cannot wait for a doctor on Earth when facing radiation, bone and muscle loss, or poor sleep. AstroVita runs on board, tracks these risks through a daily check-in, and uses NASA DONKI space-weather alerts and NASA Human Research Program guidance to adapt each astronaut’s exercise and shelter plan. This submission includes a designed dashboard prototype with sample data and a plan to connect live NASA feeds. It matters because safer, more independent crews are essential for the next frontier of exploration, and the same offline design could support remote clinics in Saudi Arabia.
details:
What it does: AstroVita is a crew health dashboard that works without a link to Earth. Astronauts complete a short daily check-in (sleep, exercise, symptoms). The app estimates exposure risk from solar events and turns it into a daily plan for exercise, rest and radiation shelter.
Benefits and impact: Crews on long missions get guidance when ground support is delayed by up to about 22 minutes. The same offline design could help remote clinics in Saudi Arabia.
What is real today: the app flow and dashboard design, shown with sample data. Live DONKI feeds, OSDR baselines and the on-board risk model are our next steps.
Tools: Python, pandas, NASA APIs (api.nasa.gov) and Figma.
What is creative: it links live space-weather alerts to a personal health plan that runs offline.
AI assistance: an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic) helped draft the text and presentation. The team reviewed all content.
dataRefs: Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight (NASA HRP)
